newsitem.title: FRANCE: ELF NAMES GAVALDA CHAIRMAN AT ELF GABON.
newsitem.headline: ELF NAMES GAVALDA CHAIRMAN AT ELF GABON.

text.p: French energy group Elf Aquitaine SA said on Thursday it had named Jean-Pierre Gavalda as chairman of its Elf Gabon unit.
Gavalda knows the group well because he was managing director of Elf Gabon until January 1, 1997 when he was made geographical director at Elf Aquitaine for Africa, a position he will keep.

Gavalda replaces Andre Tarallo, a colourful 70-year-old businessman who was instrumental in Elf's expansion in Africa but who is under judicial investigation on suspicion of receiving the proceeds of misused corporate funds. He is currently on bail of 10 million francs.
"He had reached retirement age but the recent affairs have speeded up matters somewhat," a company official said.
The chairmanship of Elf Gabon is an honorary title. Operational control is exercised by the managing director, Jean-Pierre Cordier, who was appointed in January this year.
Elf has a 58-percent stake in Elf Gabon.
Tarallo was a close collaborator of Loik Le Floch-Prigent, Elf chairman from 1988 to 1993, who is being investigated by judge Eva Joly for alleged misuse of corporate funds.
This investigation started by looking into the affairs of failed textile group Bidermann but later widened to other Elf activities.
Earlier this year, the investigation looked into bank accounts belonging to Gabon President Omar Bongo, causing a brief diplomatic spat between Gabon and France.
Papers relating to a Swiss bank account allegedly held by Tarallo for Bongo disappeared in April after a burglary at the financial police headquarters in Paris.
Le Floch-Prigent, who was head of the state railways, was put in preventive detention last year but was released in December after six months in prison.
Police raided Elf headquarters to look for documents in May. The investigation is continuing.
